description_full: AEVEX Corp. operates as a defense technology contractor and enabler of the U.S. Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) dominance strategy mission. The company operates in two segments, Tactical Systems and Global Solutions. The Tactical Systems designs and manufactures battle-tested, autonomous, modular, and attritable unmanned systems, including UAS and unmanned surface vehicles with other mission critical products. The Global Solutions provides bespoke mission solutions, including AI-enabled airborne intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), C-UAS, additive manufacturing, and specialized mission aircraft engineering, modification, and testing. The company was founded in 2020 and is based in Solana Beach, California.

financial_summary: AEVEX Corp. is a small-cap industrials business with a $706M market cap on $433M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 25% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $106M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at +12.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 13.4% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
